content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C) from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or aniline derivative). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: the amide carbonyl attached to aromatic amine (aniline). So precursor 1: aromatic aldehyde? Wait amide formation step is forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So first precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Actually the amide is attached to the phenyl ring that is part of the sulfonamide moiety? Let's parse target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl ring has a side chain /C=C/C(=O)N- aniline. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. The second phenyl has a side chain: an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl (C=C-C(=O)N-aryl). So the amide is between the α,β-unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (with phenyl sulfonyl attached) and aniline.

Thus precursor A: α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Wait the acid is the carboxylic acid after breaking amide: the side chain becomes /C=C/COOH (instead of /C=C/C(=O)N...). So the acid is attached to the second phenyl ring at same position.

So precursor A SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1

Precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N) (maybe just aniline). Could be aniline (c1ccccc1N). Good.

Now step 2: The α,β-unsaturated acid is formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (on second phenyl) and malonic acid. The aldehyde is attached to phenyl sulfonyl as well: the aromatic aldehyde is c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So precursor for step 2: aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl group: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1

And malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) as other reagent (but we may treat as external reagent not part of route). So we need to include malonic acid as a reactant? In retrosynthesis route, we can list it as a leaf node.

Thus step 2: break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus precursor after step 2: aromatic aldehyde (with sulfonyl) and malonic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide N attached to tolyl phenyl (first phenyl) is formed from amine (toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonamide formation: amine reacts with sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. In our target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl phenyl (para-methyl aniline) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give the amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl with sulfonyl chloride group (Cl-SO2-Ph). So precursor: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-Ph where phenyl has aldehyde? Actually after step 2 we have aldehyde attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl chloride would be attached to the second phenyl ring that also later gets aldehyde after step 2? In forward synthesis, we would first form sulfonyl chloride from the second phenyl (maybe with aldehyde). But the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring; the aldehyde is on that same ring. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be Cl-SO2-Ph-CHO (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). So after step 2, we have aldehyde attached to sulfonyl chloride? Actually step 2 is Doebner modification on aldehyde to give unsaturated acid. So the aldehyde is present before step 2. So the sulfonyl chloride must be present before step 2 as well. So the order of steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (last step forward) uses sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and p-toluidine to give sulfonamide. 2) Doebner modification on aldehyde (aryl sulfonyl chloride) with malonic acid to give unsaturated acid (still attached to sulfonyl chloride? Wait after Doebner, the sulfonyl group remains attached to aromatic ring; the aldehyde becomes unsaturated acid. So the sulfonyl chloride must be present before Doebner? But sulfonyl chloride is a functional group (SO2Cl). In Doebner, the aldehyde is on aromatic ring; the sulfonyl chloride is also attached to same ring. The reaction conditions may tolerate sulfonyl chloride? Possibly but for retrosynthesis we can assume it's okay.

Thus step order forward: (i) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride) -> sulfonamide. (ii) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid) -> α,β-unsaturated acid (still sulfonyl chloride? Actually after sulfonamide formation, the sulfonyl group is already attached to the second phenyl; the sulfonyl chloride is consumed to form sulfonamide, so after step (i) we have sulfonamide attached to second phenyl. Then Doebner modifies aldehyde on that phenyl to unsaturated acid. Then amide formation attaches aniline to acid.

Thus retrosynthetic order (reverse) is: target -> break amide (step 1) -> unsaturated acid + aniline. Then break C=C (Doebner) -> aldehyde + malonic acid. Then break sulfonamide -> p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde). So three steps.

Now we need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation.

We have template IDs from earlier search: For sulfonamide formation, we saw template 1313644 (Cl-[S](=O)(=O)-c) + aniline -> sulfonamide. That seems appropriate. Template ID is 1313644.

For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide), we need a template that breaks amide to give acid and amine. Search maybe with functional_groups_broken ["amide"] and formed ["aliphatic carboxylic acid","primary amines"] gave empty. Could try other criteria: functional_groups_broken ["amide"] and formed ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"] maybe.
